subject: Staging-to-Prod provisioning cadence & egress latency budget for private GPU deployment

Subject: Staging-to-Prod provisioning cadence & egress latency budget for private GPU deployment

Hi team,

Thanks again for the kickoff today. I want to capture a concrete proposal for how we move capacity from staging into production for your private VPC deployment and lock down the network/egress latency budget we should design to. High level asks from our side:

- Target sustained user request profile you expect (avg and 95th-minute peak), and any scheduled weekly/monthly batch jobs that could spike load.
- Acceptable tail latency targets we must meet in Prod (p95 and p99 for inference response time).
- Any hard egress bandwidth caps or networking constraints inside your colo/VPC we should be aware of.

Proposed initial approach (please comment):
1) Staging validation: deploy an A100-80GB 4-node cluster mirroring prod network path, run a 72-hour traffic replay with your sample production traces (we'll run warmups and KV-cache seeding).
2) Canary ramp: promote 20% of live traffic to the new pool for 48 hours, validate p95/p99 and error budgets, then 50% for 24 hours.
3) Prod commit: full cutover with an initial capacity target sized for 99th-minute peak + 30% headroom (we'll show calculations once we have your traffic numbers).

I've attached a short outline of the provisioning cadence and a checklist (initial-provisioning-outline.pdf). If you can share the expected QPM/QPS numbers and any egress caps by EOD Monday, we will produce a rightsizing table and a suggested autoscale threshold map.

Proposed next step: 30-min call Monday to lock down the numbers and agree an M.A.P.

Thanks,

Hi Ava,

Thanks — appreciate the clear plan. Quick replies to your asks:
- Expected profile: baseline ~250 req/s during business hours (US), with short 5–10 minute peaks up to ~1,200 req/s during marketing events. Night/weekend batch scoring jobs run ~2x over baseline but are rate-limited to off-peak windows.
- Latency SLAs: product team expects p95 < 160ms, p99 < 400ms end-to-end. We can tolerate short warmup degradations during canary if we have rollback hooks.
- Network: colocated data center with 25 Gbps egress per rack, but procurement prefers we keep average egress for this service below 8 Gbps to minimize cross-charges.

Procurement also asked for a formal statement of the minimum reserved capacity and a simple cost estimate for 3, 6, 12 month commits — I've looped in procurement@acmecloud.com who handles the reserved contracts.

I've attached a doc that lists our infra requirements (EnterpriseCo-infra-requirements.docx).

On Fri, Nov 20, 2026 at 13:45, ops@enterpriseco.com wrote:
> - Expected profile: baseline ~250 req/s ... peaks up to ~1,200 req/s
> - Latency SLAs: p95 < 160ms, p99 < 400ms
> - Network: 25 Gbps per rack, prefer avg egress < 8 Gbps

Thanks Sam — useful numbers. I ran a quick capacity sketch based on your numbers and some conservative assumptions (batching turned off for tail-sensitive requests, typical request size ~1.2k tokens, model variant = 1.8B optimized fp16). Summary below — attaching the detailed runbook and a short latency simulation output.

Capacity sketch (cluster-level):
- Model baseline: median token throughput per A100-80GB tile ≈ 280 tokens/sec when serving interactive requests with KV cache; that maps to roughly ~40 req/s for a 1.2k-token average generation on a single GPU.
- For a 1,200 req/s peak we need ~30 GPUs under no-batching.
- Add 35% headroom for warmups, cache misses, and burst absorption → target ~41 GPUs.
- To honor the egress cap (avg < 8 Gbps) we should:
  * enable response truncation and gzip for embeddings/payloads where possible,
  * ensure per-node egress does not exceed ~6.5 Gbps (allows rack headroom for other services).

Scaling cadence proposal:
1) Staging (4 nodes — mirror the prod node type) — run 72-hour replay. Validate KV-cache hit-rate > 85%, p95/p99 under target.
2) Canary (8 nodes) — route 20% traffic for 48h. Confirm autoscaler thresholds: scale-up at sustained 65% GPU utilization for 2m; scale-down at <30% for 5m.
3) Prod initial commit (41 GPUs target) — split across 6 racks/availability zones to reduce rack egress concentration.

Network and latency controls:
- Aim for p95 network-only hop latency < 30ms inside your VPC; keep application-layer processing p95 < 120ms to meet the 160ms end-to-end target. Reserve a p99 processing budget of 320ms (leaves ~80ms for network jitter/other infra).
- Use request-level retry gating: if p95 climbs above 170ms during canary, automatically divert to fallback smaller-model variant to maintain user experience.

Operational runbooks and artifacts attached: provisioning-runbook.pdf (contains autoscale knobs, warmup sequencing, run/revert steps), latency-sim-results.csv (simulation output for 3 traffic shapes).

Open questions:
- Do you have hard limits on per-node egress (we assumed 8 Gbps safe but your note suggests 25 Gbps per rack)?
- Are you comfortable with automatic fallback to a smaller model variant for p99 remediation?

I can join Monday's call and walk through the runbook and the math if helpful.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
